book.hardscrabble.funzang.0.page0: I am Funzang, once a brother of the quiet order. I write these pages for whoever wakes, as I did, with empty hands in a world that does not forgive.
book.hardscrabble.funzang.0.page1: Do not mistake the land for a friend. Wood will not yield to bare fists, and the night belongs to those who were here first. Gather flint: a sharp stone is the start of all wisdom.
book.hardscrabble.funzang.0.page2:
Eat little, waste nothing, sleep when you can. Patience is the only tool that never breaks.

- F.
book.hardscrabble.funzang.0.title: Funzang: On Patience
book.hardscrabble.funzang.1.page0: Copper first, then silver and gold, then iron, which asks for a hotter fire. Each metal is a door, and each door needs the key forged before it.
book.hardscrabble.funzang.1.page1: Silver is pale and soft, yet the restless dead fear it. Wear it close and their cold touch slides away. I knew a man who kept his memories only because his helmet was silver.
book.hardscrabble.funzang.1.page2:
Beyond iron lie metals with older names. I held mithril once. I will not write where; the deep keeps its own counsel.

- F.
book.hardscrabble.funzang.1.title: Funzang: On Metals
book.hardscrabble.funzang.2.page0: Under the bedrock lies another world. Its sky is stone and its sun is lava. Those who go down seldom come back the same.
book.hardscrabble.funzang.2.page1: Lava does not merely burn. It eats plate and mail alike, and hot metal shields no one from the flame. Only the hardest metal of all shrugs it off.
book.hardscrabble.funzang.2.page2:
Knowledge, like experience, can be spent. Mint it, bottle it, or carry it in your head. But spend it, for the dead carry nothing.

- F.
